title: White Sox set to call up top 100 MLB prospect Noah Schultz: Reports
content:
Towering left-handed starter Noah Schultz — ranked among MLB’s top 100 prospects in each of the past three years — is set to make his major-league debut for the Chicago White Sox during next week’s homestand, according to multiple reports.

Schultz, a 2022 first-round pick out of Oswego East High School outside of Chicago, was off to a fast start for Triple-A Charlotte. In 14 innings, Schultz had a 1.29 ERA with 19 strikeouts and just two walks. News of his impending promotion was first reported by FutureSox.com.

Standing 6-foot-10, Schultz will join Randy Johnson and Eric Hillman as the tallest left-handed pitchers in MLB history when he makes his debut. With a thin build, a scraggly mustache and a three-quarters release point, Schultz looks a little like Johnson on the mound, though Schultz doesn’t have Johnson’s power arsenal. Coming into this season, one of the biggest knocks on Schultz was that he wasn’t missing enough bats, especially for someone with his height and ability to run his fastball up to 99 mph.

Primarily a sinker/slider pitcher, Schultz struck out 76 in 73 innings last season in a year split between Double-A Birmingham and Triple-A Charlotte. His K/9 dropped from 11.7 in 2024 to 9.4 and his BB/9 more than doubled, going from 2.4 to 5.5. He went from being ranked 20th in The Athletic’s 2025 top 100 list to 95 going into this season.

Schultz was limited to 73 innings last season by a patella injury that may have contributed to his struggles on the mound. Injuries have been an issue for Schultz during his minor-league career, as he’s dealt with shoulder and flexor tendon injuries in the past and has yet to exceed 100 innings in any one season.

This season, Schultz has looked like a different pitcher in the early going. He’s throwing strikes again and has significantly increased the usage of his cut fastball against right-handed hitters. He struggled against right-handers last season, allowing an .890 OPS, but has given up just three hits and one walk in 32 plate appearances against right-handers so far this season. He’s also recorded 10 strikeouts in those 32 PAs and walked just one. He’s always been tough against left-handed hitters and that has carried over into this season, as he’s struck out nine lefties in 13 PAs against them.

Schultz can run his fastball up to 99, but generally sits in the 93-97 mph range. He relies heavily on his sinker, which helps him induce a lot of ground balls. Even in a down season last year, he had a 58 percent ground-ball rate. His slider is an above-average pitch and has been especially devastating against left-handed hitters. He also features a four-seam fastball and a changeup.

The White Sox had an opening in their rotation after they sent down 2025 All-Star Shane Smith earlier this week. Smith, who was the team’s Opening Day starter, had a 10.80 ERA in three starts this season and had yet to complete the fourth inning in any of his outings. His turn in the rotation was on Sunday, but the White Sox are going with an opener in their series finale against the Kansas City Royals. Schultz is expected to make his debut on Tuesday in the series opener against the Tampa Bay Rays.
